headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with overbought momentum as whales pull coins off exchanges and ETF inflows split by asset.
paragraphs: The regime is orderly on the major assets. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages; Dogecoin and Cardano do not. No golden crosses are live across the board, which means the longer-term trend structure, while above the intermediate line, has not yet confirmed a fresh acceleration. The picture is a market in a sustained recovery but not yet in textbook new-cycle confirmation. Bitcoin is up 21.7% over the month, Ethereum up 34.5%, and Solana up 40.8%: all three have compressed the damage from their 12-month highs, though each remains well below (Bitcoin 36.8% down, Ethereum 46.8%, Solana 57.1%). The compression is real; the deep hole is also real.

Momentum across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana is stretched. RSI-14 on Bitcoin sits at 72.6, on Ethereum at 72.8, and on Solana at 76.0, all above 70 and reading overbought in the classical sense. MACD is above signal on every major asset except Cardano, confirming that the recent gains are riding an accelerating trend rather than dying into exhaustion. The tension is not hidden: strong momentum paired with elevated RSI creates a state where any reversal has room to run downward. Conversely, a market that reaches these RSI levels and holds them without rolling over is often the one that keeps moving. Cardano is the outlier, with MACD below signal, RSI at 54.4, and a price still below its 200-day line. It is the only major asset without confirmation of the broader recovery.

Funding on the long side is expensive across Bitcoin and Ethereum. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding rate stands at 0.0036 percent (4.0 percent annualized), and Ethereum's at 0.0087 percent (9.6 percent annualized), both positive and both crowded enough to attract shorts. Open interest on Bitcoin is USD 2.21 billion with a long-to-short ratio of 1.19; on Ethereum, USD 1.59 billion at 1.2. The asymmetry is telling: longs are being paid for in both markets, yet the recent liquidation roll shows shorts getting wiped far harder. Over the last 20 hours on Bitcoin, 702 liquidations fired with shorts taking USD 5.44 million in damage versus longs at USD 95,689. On Ethereum over 20 hours, 1,276 liquidations and shorts at USD 8.82 million against longs at USD 1.04 million. Funding is inviting leverage; liquidation flow is punishing it. Solana and Dogecoin show negative funding (shorts paying longs), a sign that the crowd's eagerness has limits even in a recovery.

Stablecoin float sits at USD 309.76 billion, up 1.36 percent over the month, a modest buildup of dry powder. Bitcoin ETF flows split the narrative: on 28 Aug (the latest reported day), there was an outflow of USD 201.9 million, but over the last five sessions the net inflow totaled USD 924.5 million, showing only one same-direction day. The disagreement between the day and the five-session window indicates a recent pause, not a reversal. Ethereum ETH ETF flows, by contrast, are aligned: inflow of USD 102.1 million on 28 Aug paired with USD 815.7 million over five sessions and ten same-direction days of inflows. The Ethereum frame is steady; the Bitcoin frame is choppy on the margin.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours show USD 176.19 million moving off exchanges, driven by Bitcoin withdrawals from Kraken and Coinbase Institutional. The weekly lens, however, reveals a deeper pattern: week ending Aug 16, USD 441 million moved onto exchanges; week ending Aug 23, USD 946 million onto exchanges; week ending Aug 30 (current), USD 775 million onto exchanges. Three weeks of net inflow onto exchanges followed by two days of outflow. The larger whales are cycling: they brought coins in through late August and have begun testing exit windows, even as the shorter-term rebound tempts retail back in. Fear and Greed sits at 69 (Greed), within a 30-day range of 25 to 74, confirming the crowd is confident but not euphoric.

Watch the durability of momentum above RSI 70 on the majors, especially Bitcoin and Ethereum, as the condition that would confirm whether this is a sustained trend or a bounce into resistance. Monitor whether Ethereum ETF inflows persist in the same-direction streak they have held for ten days, and whether Bitcoin ETF flows return to net positive (they have not been negative for multiple days). A rollover in funding rates or a sharp liquidation of longs would signal a change in positioning fragility. On the weekly whale flow front, track whether the large inflows onto exchanges last week reverse into sustained outflows, which would align with a conviction move higher, or whether they resume, which would indicate uncertainty even among large holders.
